arxiv-2102-12858.title: Emotion-Aware, Emotion-Agnostic, or Automatic: Corpus Creation Strategies to Obtain Cognitive Event Appraisal Annotations
arxiv-2102-12858.creator: Jan Hofmann, Enrica Troiano, Roman Klinger
arxiv-2102-12858.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jan Hofmann, Enrica Troiano, Roman Klinger. Appraisal theories explain how the cognitive evaluation of an event leads to a particular emotion. In contrast to theories of basic emotions or affect (valence/arousal), this theory has not received a lot of attention in natural language processing. Yet, in psychology it has been proven powerful: Smith and Ellsworth 1985 showed that the appraisal dimensions attention , certainty , anticipated effort , pleasantness , responsibility / control and situational control discriminate between (at least) 15 emotion classes.

arxiv-2204-03930.title: From Rewriting to Remembering: Common Ground for Conversational QA Models
arxiv-2204-03930.creator: Marco Del Tredici, Xiaoyu Shen, Gianni Barlacchi, Bill Byrne, Adrià de Gispert
arxiv-2204-03930.description: Abstract In conversational QA, models have to leverage information in previous turns to answer upcoming questions. Current approaches, such as Question Rewriting, struggle to extract relevant information as the conversation unwinds. We introduce the Common Ground (CG), an approach to accumulate conversational information as it emerges and select the relevant information at every turn.

arxiv-2209-05605.title: NGC 3314a/b and NGC 3312: Ram pressure stripping in Hydra I Cluster substructure
arxiv-2209-05605.creator: Kelley M. Hess, Ralf Kotulla, Hao Chen, Claude Carignan, John S. Gallagher, T. H. Jarrett, Renée C. Kraan-Korteweg
arxiv-2209-05605.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kelley M. Hess, Ralf Kotulla, Hao Chen, Claude Carignan, John S. Gallagher, T. H. Jarrett, Renée C. Kraan-Korteweg. Cluster substructure and ram pressure stripping in individual galaxies are among the primary evidence for the ongoing growth of galaxy clusters as they accrete galaxies and groups from their surroundings.

arxiv-2210-15509.title: On Tsirelson pairs of C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -algebras Thanks: I. Goldbring was partially supported by NSF grant DMS-2504477. B. Hart was partially supported by the NSERC
arxiv-2210-15509.creator: Isaac Goldbring and Bradd Hart
arxiv-2210-15509.description: Abstract . We introduce the notion of a Tsirelson pair of C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -algebras, which is a pair of C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -algebras for which the space of quantum strategies obtained by using states on the minimal tensor product of the pair is dense in the space of quantum strategies obtained by using states on the maximal tensor product.

arxiv-2302-02413.title: Degenerate Schrödinger equations with irregular potentials Thanks: The authors are supported by the FWO Odysseus 1 grant G.0H94.18N:Analysis and Partial Differential Equations and by the Methusalem programme of the Ghent University Special Research Fund(BOF)(Grant number 01M01021). J. Delgado is als
arxiv-2302-02413.creator: Duván Cardona, Marianna Chatzakou, Julio Delgado, Michael Ruzhansky
arxiv-2302-02413.description: Abstract . In this work we investigate a class of degenerate Schrödinger equations associated to degenerate elliptic operators with irregular potentials on ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} by introducing a suitable Hörmander metric g g and a g g -weight m m . We establish the well-posedness for the corresponding degenerate Schrödinger and degenerate parabolic equations.

arxiv-2304-01968.description: Abstract KA-TP-04-2023 P3H-23-020 OUTP-23-03P LHCHWG-2022-004 October 17, 2024 LHC Higgs Working Group a a a https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/LHCPhysics/LHCHWG Public Note Effective Field Theory descriptions of Higgs boson pair production Lina Alasfar 1 b b b alasfarl@physik.hu-berlin.de , Luca Cadamuro 2 c c c luca.cadamuro@cern.ch , Christina Dimitriadi 3,4 d d d christina.dimitriadi@cern.ch , Arnaud Ferrari 4 e e e arnaud.ferrari@physics.uu.

arxiv-2312-03758.title: Stock Movement and Volatility Prediction from Tweets, Macroeconomic Factors and Historical Prices
arxiv-2312-03758.creator: Shengkun Wang, YangXiao Bai, Taoran Ji, Kaiqun Fu, Linhan Wang, Chang-Tien Lu
arxiv-2312-03758.description: Abstract Predicting stock market is vital for investors and policymakers, acting as a barometer of the economic health. We leverage social media data, a potent source of public sentiment, in tandem with macroeconomic indicators as government-compiled statistics, to refine stock market predictions. However, prior research using tweet data for stock market prediction faces three challenges.

arxiv-2402-02858.title: Deep autoregressive density nets vs neural ensembles for model-based offline reinforcement learning
arxiv-2402-02858.creator: Abdelhakim Benechehab, Albert Thomas, Balázs Kégl
arxiv-2402-02858.description: Abstract We consider the problem of offline reinforcement learning where only a set of system transitions is made available for policy optimization. Following recent advances in the field, we consider a model-based reinforcement learning algorithm that infers the system dynamics from the available data and performs policy optimization on imaginary model rollouts.

arxiv-2403-13736.title: Statistical Confidence in Mining Power Estimates for PoW Blockchains
arxiv-2403-13736.creator: Mary Milad, Christina Ovezik, Dimitris Karakostas, Daniel W. Woods
arxiv-2403-13736.description: Abstract The security of blockchain systems depends on the distribution of mining power across participants. If sufficient mining power is controlled by one entity, they can force their own version of events. This may allow them to double spend coins, for example.

arxiv-2410-13804.title: BenTo : Benchmark Task Reduction with In-Context Transferability
arxiv-2410-13804.creator: Hongyu Zhao, Ming Li, Lichao Sun, Tianyi Zhou
arxiv-2410-13804.description: Abstract Evaluating large language models (LLMs) is costly: it requires the generation and examination of LLM outputs on a large-scale benchmark of various tasks. This paper investigates how to efficiently reduce the tasks used to benchmark LLMs without affecting the evaluation quality.

arxiv-2410-22273.title: Driving forces in cell migration and pattern formation in a soft tissue
arxiv-2410-22273.creator: Amabile Tatone, Filippo Recrosi, Giuseppe Tomassetti
arxiv-2410-22273.description: Abstract We give a description of cell diffusion in a soft tissue, paying special attention to the coupling of force, matter, and microforce balance laws through a suitable dissipation principle. To this end, we cast our framework into a multi-level schematics, comprising both kinematics and kinetics, based on a characterization of the free energy.

arxiv-2411-19911.title: Interacting Dark Sector (ETHOS n = 0 n=0 ): Cosmological Constraints from SPT Cluster Abundance with DES and HST Weak Lensing Data
arxiv-2411-19911.creator: A. Mazoun, S. Bocquet, J. J. Mohr, M. Garny, H. Rubira, M. Klein, L. E. Bleem, S. Grandis, T. Schrabback, M. Aguena, S. Allam, S. W. Allen, O. Alves, F. Andrade-Oliveira, D. Brooks, A. Carnero Rosell, M. Carrasco Kind, J. Carretero, M. Costanzi, L. N. da Costa, T. M. Davis, S. Desai, J. De Vicente,
arxiv-2411-19911.description: Abstract We use galaxy cluster abundance measurements from the South Pole Telescope (SPT) enhanced by Multi-Component Matched Filter (MCMF) confirmation and complemented with mass information obtained using weak-lensing data from Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3) and targeted Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations for probing deviations from the cold dark matter paradigm.

arxiv-2506-19785.title: Learning Task Belief Similarity with Latent Dynamics for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2506-19785.creator: Menglong Zhang, Fuyuan Qian
arxiv-2506-19785.description: Abstract Meta-reinforcement learning requires utilizing prior task distribution information obtained during exploration to rapidly adapt to unknown tasks. The efficiency of an agent’s exploration hinges on accurately identifying the current task. Recent Bayes-Adaptive Deep RL approaches often rely on reconstructing the environment’s reward signal, which is challenging in sparse reward settings, leading to suboptimal exploitation.

arxiv-2508-13208.title: Modeling GRNs with a Probabilistic Categorical Framework
arxiv-2508-13208.creator: Yiyang Jia, Zheng Wei, Zheng Yang, Guohong Peng, [0.5em] Tokyo City University, [0.5em] Correspondence: kaiyou@tcu.ac.jp
arxiv-2508-13208.description: Abstract Understanding the complex and stochastic nature of Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) remains a central challenge in systems biology. Existing modeling paradigms often struggle to effectively capture the intricate, multi-factor regulatory logic and to rigorously manage the dual uncertainties of network structure and kinetic parameters. In response, this work introduces the Probabilistic Categorical GRN (PC-GRN) framework.

arxiv-2510-16437.title: Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement for Spatial Audio - Spatial-VisualVoice and the MAVE Database
arxiv-2510-16437.creator: Danielle Yaffe, Ferdinand Campe, Prachi Sharma, Dorothea Kolossa, Boaz Rafaely
arxiv-2510-16437.description: Abstract Audio-visual speech enhancement (AVSE) has been found to be particularly useful at low signal-to-noise (SNR) ratios due to the immunity of the visual features to acoustic noise. However, a significant gap exists in AVSE methods tailored to enhance spatial audio under low-SNR conditions. The latter is of growing interest with augmented reality applications.

arxiv-2602-05400.title: OPUS: Towards Efficient and Principled Data Selection in Large Language Model Pre-training in Every Iteration
arxiv-2602-05400.creator: Shaobo Wang Xuan Ouyang Tianyi Xu Yuzheng Hu Jialin Liu, Guo Chen Tianyu Zhang Junhao Zheng Kexin Yang Xingzhang Ren, Dayiheng Liu Linfeng Zhang
arxiv-2602-05400.description: Abstract As high-quality public text approaches exhaustion, a phenomenon known as the Data Wall ( 46 ) , pre-training is shifting from more tokens to better tokens . However, existing methods either rely on heuristic static filters that ignore training dynamics, or use dynamic yet optimizer-agnostic criteria based on raw gradients.

pmc-11325716.description: IntroductionWhen medically indicated, caesarean section (CS) can be a life-saving intervention for mothers and their newborns. This study assesses the prevalence of CS and its associated factors, focussing on inequalities between rural and urban areas in Nigeria.MethodsWe disaggregated the Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey 2018 and performed analyses separately for Nigeria’s overall, rural, and urban residences.

pmc-13616636.title: Bioregulatory periodontal medicine: could the molecular networks, inflammation and system biology modify the auto-regulatory capacity of the patients?
pmc-13616636.creator: María Carolina Varas-Reyes, Bertha Arelly Carrillo-Ávila, Victor Martínez-Aguilar, Marco Antonio Álvarez-Pérez, Jaime Díaz-Zúñiga, Samanta Melgar-Rodríguez
pmc-13616636.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe traditional healthcare model, focused on symptom management, has shown limitations in addressing chronic diseases. In response, Bioregulatory Systems Medicine (BrSM) has emerged, an approach that promotes the body’s self-regulation through multi-component drug and phytotherapeutic treatments. Its potential application in dentistry, particularly in periodontitis, has spurred the study of various natural molecules with the potential to prevent or reduce bone resorption.

pmc-13667988.title: Systemic Inflammation and Nutritional Index as a prognostic marker in endometrial cancer
pmc-13667988.creator: Nagihan Kolkıran, Atike Pınar Erdoğan, Mustafa Şahbazlar, Mustafa Şahin, Ferhat Ekinci
pmc-13667988.description: The clinical course of endometrial cancer exhibits substantial variability, underscoring the need for additional biomarkers to enhance risk stratification accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic utility of a novel composite index, integrating systemic inflammatory and nutritional parameters, herein termed the Systemic Inflammation and Nutritional Index (SINI), in patients diagnosed with endometrial cancer.

uslaw-usc-t10-s254.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s254.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part I (Organization And General Military Powers); Chapter 13 (Insurrection). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whenever the President considers it necessary to use the militia or the armed forces under this chapter, he shall, by proclamation, immediately order the insurgents to disperse and retire peaceably to their abodes within a limited time.
